title: Beau-Koo Jack, Teddy Wilson's arrangements and unused talent
summary: They recall Roy and Jonah singing Beau-Koo Jack off Louis's record, and Teddy Wilson's scoring of Bix's solo.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well, Horace Henderson's band... I remember once you and Jonah at Ryan's, singing "Beau-Koo Jack."
But that was taken right off Louis' record.

Right off his solo, yeah. But you see, you must understand, as great as it was, it wasn't my thing. Like I said, I played what I needed to play to survive. Yeah, man! You do that (?) on "Beau-Koo Jack". [SINGS 16 BARS] That was a good thing there.
Teddy Wilson wrote Bix's solo on "Sweet Sue" out for the big band.
For his big band? - for Speed Webb!
Yeah, we had that. Yeah. Teddy wrote nice, too, man. All those cats could write good. The talent was

there. Man, the talent was there. There was just nowhere for it to go, you know. They had the (?) playing. Damn shame, man. To think what cats make today, those Rock-and-Roll cats. Isn't that ridiculous? Some of the baseball players! Think about those cats.
